q1_issues.issue: The appositive typing (Member ken_goldstein economist) is left bare, but the appositive rule gives such a typing atom the host clause's wrapper, and the host clause "said" is past.
(Member sk_end_1 end) types the definite "the end of the recession" inside the seal, but a definite referent's typing projects to top level — as sk_recession_1's correctly does in the same parse.

"almost a year and a half" is encoded as the symmetric (ParticleFromNormal 1.5 0.15), but "almost" is a one-sided upper-bound hedge and is not one of the approximators whose sigma band the instruction set defines.

q2_gaps: A proper-noun modifier naming an affiliation on a common-noun head ("Conference Board economist Ken Goldstein"): both entities are emitted but no licensed head relates the person to the named organization.

One-sided approximators ("almost", "nearly", "just over"): only the symmetric hedges about/around/approximately and roughly have a defined encoding, and there is no bounded variant of BeforeBy to carry an upper-bounded gap.
A discourse/phasal adverb ("finally"): the aspectual-particle set is closed at again/still/already/yet, and Manner would mis-slot it, so the word is silently lost.
Direct quotation as a speech verb's complement: the propositional-attitude section covers only a finite "that"-clause, so nothing says how verbatim quoted speech is recorded.
notes: The non-factive seal under say's Theme, the (To …) oblique for the prepositional verb "points to", the (Of …) nominalization argument, and the bare temporal-anchor treatment of the end event-noun all follow the instruction set. Projecting the definite Leading Economic Index and recession out of the seal while keeping the indefinite recovery inside is exactly right.
